title: Post-Trabeculectomy Masterclass: The Early Post-Op Matrix
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to managing the early postoperative period after glaucoma filtration surgery. Focuses on the critical relationship between IOP, Anterior Chamber (AC) depth, and bleb morphology to differentiate surgical success from sight-threatening complications.

sections.title: Differential: Pupillary Block vs. Ciliary Block
Management of the Failing Bleb
content: Step 1: Clinical Assessment - Rule out internal ostium blockage via gonioscopy.
Step 2: Digital Pressure (Buratto's Maneuver) - Apply pressure through lower lid to force aqueous through flap.
Step 3: Laser Suture Lysis (LSL) - Use Hoskins lens to cut 10-0 nylon flap sutures (typically days 3-14).
Step 4: Pharmacological Modulation - Subconjunctival 5-FU (5mg in 0.1ml) to inhibit fibroblast proliferation.
Step 5: Bleb Needling - Break episcleral adhesions using a 27G or 30G needle, often with MMC (0.02%).

sections.title: Red Flags: Post-Op Emergencies
content: Blebitis: Milky/White bleb + localized inflammation.
Bleb-Related Endophthalmitis: Hypopyon + Severe pain + Vitritis.
Suprachoroidal Hemorrhage: Severe pain + Hard eye + Loss of red reflex.
Hypotony Maculopathy: Chorioretinal folds + Macular edema (IOP < 5).

sections.title: Surgical Landmarks for Trabeculectomy
content: Scleral Flap: 3x4mm rectangular or triangular, 50% depth.
Internal Ostium: 1.5x2mm block removed with Kelly Punch.
Iridectomy: Basal, wider than the ostium to prevent blockage.
Suture Tension: Titrated to allow 1 drop/5 seconds of flow at 20mmHg.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Residents
content: Never perform digital pressure if you suspect a wound leak.
Always use Atropine 1% BID in 'shallow AC' cases until the cause is confirmed.
A 'Large, Low' bleb is usually better than a 'Small, High' bleb.
If IOP is high on Day 1, check the ostium with a Gonio lens immediately.

sections.title: Landmark Studies
sections.content: The Tube Versus Trabeculectomy (TVT) study and the Primary Tube Versus Trabeculectomy (PTVT) study have provided critical insights. The PTVT study showed that at 3 years, trabeculectomy with MMC had a higher success rate compared to tube shunts in primary surgical eyes, though complications like hypotony were more frequent in the trabeculectomy group.
